topic: Greene conservative farthest-depth Hierarchical-Z (Hi-Z) pyramid vs average-mip false occlusion popping rig
topic_zh: Greene 保守最远深度层次深度金字塔（Hi-Z）遮挡剔除对比均值深度 Mip 门缝误剔除闪崩
scope: Deterministic Ned Greene et al. (SIGGRAPH 1993) conservative farthest-depth Hierarchical-Z (Hi-Z) mip reduction (z_HiZ = max(z_0..z_63)) versus naive box-average depth mipmapping and brute-force 64-pixel full-resolution tile scanning across 17 object depth stations (z_obj in [6.0, 46.0] m) behind a 4-pixel doorway slit. No neural visibility prediction execution.

good_fit: Two-phase GPU-driven cluster and instance occlusion culling in UE5 Nanite, Frostbite, and Unity GPU Resident Drawer
Explaining why standard box-average generateMipmap() on a depth buffer causes 94.12% false occlusion popping through doorways and fences
Reducing each 2×2 Hi-Z mip level with conservative farthest-depth (max in linear Z, min in Reversed-Z)
Replacing 64-pixel full-resolution bounding-box depth scans with a single O(1) Hi-Z mip lookup
not_for: View-frustum-only culling where depth buffer occlusion is never tested (use Gribb-Hartmann frustum planes instead)
Color texture mipmapping where box/Kaiser averaging is desired for anti-aliasing
Translucent glass windows that do not write to the occluder depth buffer
